sentence: This project studies how cells use gene expression and tension to guide shape changes through directed cellular movements.
This project builds medicinal chemistry workflows that improve small-molecule hits for underexplored biological targets.
This project tests curative gene therapies that target the hepatitis B virus in infected cells, using an affordable humanized mouse model.
This project adds fluorescence lifetime imaging to colonoscopy to give real-time biochemical information about lesions and help detect colorectal cancer.
This project studies how genes control the changes in cell shape and position that differ by sex during growth and development.
This project tests whether an immune regulatory drug can reduce chronic inflammation and block or reverse neurodegeneration after repeated mild traumatic brain injury.
This project develops imaging methods that make pediatric brain MRI faster and need less gadolinium injection, so less sedation or anesthesia is needed.
This project tries to find out why the personality trait conscientiousness protects against cognitive impairment and dementia.
This project studies how radiotherapy followed by an mRNA-mediated immunotherapeutic helps T cell immunity fight pancreatic cancer in the tumor microenvironment.
This project tries to find out how the mitochondrial dicarboxylate carrier controls liver gluconeogenic metabolism in normal and type 2 diabetes states.
This project studies how reflux injury and repair lead to Barrett's esophagus and its progression to esophageal adenocarcinoma.
This project builds services that give HIV researchers access to technology in sequencing, imaging, immunophenotyping, and drug discovery.
This project studies how nerves sense lung tumors and shape tumor growth, using mouse models of lung cancer.
This project studies the thalamocortical circuits that link chronic pain and sleep disturbances, using optogenetics and in vivo imaging.
This project manages and analyzes clinical, genomic, imaging and pathology data to help find biomarkers and improve lymphoma outcomes.
This project tests whether chimeric antigen receptor T cells can protect transplant recipients from leukemia relapse and graft-versus-host disease.
This project builds a mass spectrometry platform that uses accelerated droplet chemistry to tell apart isomeric lipids and saccharides.
This project studies how telomere stress affects hematopoietic stem cells and how telomere damage relates to clonal hematopoiesis.
This project builds software that automatically detects and measures amyloid related imaging abnormalities in images of Alzheimer's patients during treatment.
This project tries to find out how clonal hematopoiesis can be redirected toward normal hematopoiesis and stopped from progressing.
